forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

news_drafts.headline: Wirral schools funding deficit forecast to reach £120m by end of 2026/27, funded by borrowing
news_drafts.lead:
Wirral Council expects its schools funding deficit to reach £120m by the end of 2026/27 and is paying for it by borrowing. The figure is in the council's prudential indicators (the limits and measures every council must publish to show its borrowing is affordable), which go to full Council on 12 October. The deficit is an overspend on the dedicated schools grant, the government grant that funds schools, mainly on support for children with special educational needs.

The papers say the council is meeting the deficit through capital borrowing rather than from its day-to-day budget, and describe it as continuing to grow. As a result, its borrowing is above its capital financing requirement (CFR), the total it has spent on long-lived assets and not yet paid for, in effect its underlying need to borrow. At 31 March 2026 borrowing was £640.335m against a requirement of £565.087m. By 31 March 2029 it is estimated at £744.893m against £582.922m.

The government has announced a High Needs Stability Grant, payable in autumn 2026, equal to 90% of the deficit at the end of 2025/26, which stood at £66.410m. High needs is the part of school funding for children with special needs. The council says the grant "will not be sufficient to bring the Council's external debt back below its CFR", and expects borrowing to remain above the requirement at the end of 2026/27.

news_drafts.headline: Merseyside Pension Fund audit unqualified pending £13.6m investment variance resolution
news_drafts.lead: Grant Thornton's audit of the Merseyside Pension Fund is anticipated to result in an unqualified opinion on its financial statements, subject to completion of outstanding work. However, auditors have identified a £13.6m difference between the fund's valuations of complex investments, known as Level 3 assets, and confirmations from external managers as at 31 March 2026. The fund's accounts, with net assets of £12,189m, do not adjust for this variance. Management asserts the difference is immaterial both quantitatively and qualitatively, sitting above the £7.3m reporting threshold but below performance materiality of £109.5m. Auditors are still awaiting three Level 3 investment confirmations from fund managers and one related party declaration before finalising their opinion. The audit fee is proposed at £128,262.
news_drafts.paper_title: 26Sept PB Audit Findings Report for MPF

news_drafts.headline: Wirral pension fund budget jumps 57% as new investment company launches
news_drafts.lead: The Merseyside Pension Fund's administration budget will rise to £38.5m in 2026/27, up from £24.5m in the previous year, the Pensions Committee heard today. The £14m increase is primarily driven by set-up costs and management fees for Northern LGPS, a new FCA-regulated investment company managing pension schemes across the Northern authorities. The committee also authorized the Director of Pensions to provide regulatory capital for Northern LGPS as determined by the Financial Conduct Authority's requirements. In separate audit findings, Grant Thornton expects to give the fund an unqualified opinion on its 2025/26 accounts, though a prior-year recommendation to implement monitoring of the Oracle Fusion financial system for unauthorized activity remains in progress.

findings.paper_title: Appendix G: Capital Programme Scheme Updates
findings.headline: Public Sector Decarbonisation Scheme Phase 4: council 14% participant cost exposure with planning delay at one site
findings.detail: The scheme is being delivered by Liverpool City Region Combined Authority and will invoice the Council for its 14% participant contribution. Work at Landican Cemetery is nearly complete awaiting electrical clearance for solar PV connection. Wirral Country Park site has been delayed by a planning objection; resubmission is in progress following onsite consultation. The contractor is completing detailed surveys at eight other council sites for RIBA Stage 4 design.
findings.matters: The council's cost exposure as a participant in an externally-managed scheme requires ongoing tracking, and planning delays can affect overall programme cost and timing.
findings.figures: 14% participant cost share, sites affected: Landican Cemetery, Wirral Country Park, Wallasey Town Hall, Leasowe Leisure Centre, West Kirby Concourse, The Oval, Floral Pavilion, Birkenhead Central Library, Williamson Art Gallery
findings.quote: The Council is expected to pay 14% of total costs as a participant contribution

findings.paper_title: Appendix G: Capital Programme Scheme Updates
findings.headline: School Condition Allocation budget slippage from legal challenge, programme review and capacity constraints
findings.detail: The SCA budget experienced slippage from multiple causes: a legal challenge, programme review prompted by headteacher concerns, and limited Assets Team capacity to develop schemes. Progress is now being made: the Joseph Paxton Campus roof scheme has commenced with phase 2 approved; heating system replacements at three primary schools are designed and scheduled for summer 2026; outstanding SEND Pod works are scheduled for summer break.
findings.matters: Significant programme delays with multiple underlying causes indicate resource and governance pressures, but evidence of remedial action shows management focus and delivery pathway.
findings.figures: Three schools with heating systems scheduled Q2 2026: West Kirby Primary, Higher Bebington Juniors, Bidston Primary
findings.quote: Slippage in this budget area has been to a number of reasons including legal challenge, programme review linked to issues raised by Headteachers and capacity in the Assets Team to work up schemes

findings.paper_title: Appendix G: Capital Programme Scheme Updates
findings.headline: Borough Yard regeneration contract timescales extended to refine drainage strategy
findings.detail: The Council has progressed through a Pre-Construction Services Agreement with John Sisk & Sons but has extended timescales for entering into the main construction contract and grant funding agreements to refine the drainage strategy for the site. Grant drawdown is now expected from Q3 2026/27 onwards rather than earlier quarters.
findings.matters: Timeline extensions to construction contracts and grant drawdown schedules affect cash flow planning and delivery forecasting across multiple future years.
findings.figures: Q3 2026/27 expected start for grant drawdown
findings.quote: The timescales to entering into the main construction contract and grant funding agreements have been extended to refine the drainage strategy for the site

findings.paper_title: Appendix G: Capital Programme Scheme Updates
findings.headline: Mosslands School construction remained on schedule in Q1 2026/27 with major groundworks completed
findings.detail: The new school build is progressing on schedule through Q1. Major grounds work for phase 1 has been completed and a PE and outdoor games area has been prepared. Steel erection for the sports hall is beginning with a signing ceremony planned for 26th June 2026. Final stage DfE payments have been made in line with section 151 agreements.
findings.matters: A major DfE-funded scheme remaining on schedule and maintaining payment milestone alignment demonstrates delivery capability and preserves cash flow.
findings.quote: Construction of the new Mosslands School has remained on schedule during Quarter 1 of 2026/27

findings.paper_title: Appendix G: Capital Programme Scheme Updates
findings.headline: Birkenhead Waterfront regeneration programme £0.500 million slippage into future years
findings.detail: Capital scheme delays on the wider waterfront regeneration have caused approximately £0.500 million to slip into future years. Battle of the Atlantic experienced a delay gaining planning approval before starting on site in April 2026. The Priory is out to tender for a contractor following procurement and resourcing delays. Woodside Ferry Pontoon has been completed with all funds spent.
findings.matters: This is a material variance in the capital programme affecting year-on-year delivery targets and cash flow forecasting into future financial years.
findings.quote: These delays have caused the slippage of approx. £0.500 million that will be slipped into future years

daily_post.headline: Fund investment performance in 2025/26 exceeded forecast by £929 million, with total assets rising to £12.2 billion.
daily_post.lead: Better-than-forecast investment returns reduce pressure for future contribution increases and demonstrate effective asset management, supporting the long-term sustainability of pension obligations and employer costs.
